title: uv engine installs an UNPINNED ComfyUI, then stamps it with the pinned version (LTX dies on macOS + Linux)
description: Measured live on the rented M4 2026-07-31. engine/.mpi_engine_version reads 0.28.0 while engine/ComfyUI_macos/comfyui_version.py reads 0.29.0. _provisionUvEngine builds its `comfy install` args at routes/engine.js:405-407 and passes NO version flag, so comfy-cli clones whatever is current on master; routes/engine.js:538-544 then writes config.engine.version (the pin) into the stamp regardless of what actually landed. THE DRIFT IS SELF-CONCEALING: /engine/version-check (routes/engine.js:613-620) compares that stamp against COMFY_VERSION, both read 0.28.0, they match, and no repair is ever offered - a 0.29.0 tree reports as a healthy 0.28.0 install forever. OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE: our pinned ComfyUI-LTXVideo commit 4f45fd6c cannot import against 0.29.0 - `cannot import name 'interleaved_freqs_cis' from 'comfy.ldm.lightricks.model'`. Verified on the box that core 0.29.0 does not define it and ComfyUI-LTXVideo/embeddings_connector.py:13 imports it (used at :258); the core change is ComfyUI #15056 'Use comfy kitchen rope functions in ltx models'. So LTX VIDEO IS DEAD ON EVERY LOCAL UV ENGINE - macOS AND Linux. Windows is unaffected because its prebuilt-archive path is genuinely pinned. TIME-ACTIVATED: while 0.28.0 was current the unpinned install happened to produce the right thing; it broke the day 0.29.0 shipped, which is why it has never been seen. FIX AGREED WITH THE USER (2026-07-31): bump FORWARD, do not pin back - 1.3.0 is to carry ComfyUI 0.29.2. Pass an explicit version to `comfy install` (comfy-cli supports --version and --commit, confirmed from its own --help on the box); stamp the version READ BACK from comfyui_version.py, never the pin; bump core in dev_configs/node_lock.json + dev_configs/system_dependencies.json; bump ComfyUI-LTXVideo and the frontend pins (ours: comfyui-frontend-package 1.45.21, workflow-templates 0.11.9) to match; sweep the other 14 pinned nodes for 0.29 compatibility. NOTE node_lock.json ALSO drives the RunPod Pod image build (mpi-ci/cubric-vision-pod), so the dual-engine clause of the root-cause rule applies - decide the remote half with the user, do not fix only the local twin. TEST ORDER SET BY THE USER: install on the Windows dev PC bench first to shake out 0.29 breakage, then the rented Mac, then Linux as a stretch (that ThinkPad cannot boot ComfyUI at all - MPI-415 - so it can only ever be a partial signal). Evidence: tasks/MPI-370/validation.md section 'TWO NEW DEFECTS FOUND AT FIRST BOOT'. BLOCKS the 1.3.0 publish.
